title: Fade-recovery surge pulse scratch
content:
Goal: quick notes on a "fade -> recovery" pattern I observed in the field simulator. This is a scratchpad — rough timelines, raw numbers, and first-pass hypotheses. NOT for execs.

Background:
- Saw a repeated pattern in replayed client mix: short intense pulse (10s-30s) then a 'fade' where throughput drops ~25% for 60–120s before returning to baseline.
- This differs from simple cold-cache behavior: model KV hit stays ~stable, GPU utilization dips, and queue depth shows a long, low-amplitude tail.
- Repro on local cluster with fleet of 4 A100 replicas and our standard batching runtime (commit: runtime@f2b7c).

Experiment setup (baseline run):
- Model: rwd-7b-quant-8k
- Replicas: 4 x a100 (32GB)
- Concurrency per replica: 8
- Batching: dynamic, max_batch_size=128, batch_timeout_ms=6
- Ingress: synthetic trace (heavy tail mixes) replayed at peak QPS=420
- Telemetry: queue_depth, gpu_util, kv_cache_hit, p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec.

Observed pattern (single-run excerpt):
Timestamp window (s)   QPS_in   queue_depth   gpu_util   kv_hit%   p99_latency_ms
0-10                   420      12            96%        89%       48
10-20                  420      18            98%        88%       55
20-30                  1200     90            100%       86%       210   <-- short pulse (client burst)
30-40                  420      65            70%        87%       430   <-- fade begins, GPU util drops, latency spikes
40-140                 420      8             42%        86%       210   <-- sustained degraded GPU util for ~100s
140-170                420      10            92%        89%       52   <-- recovery to baseline

Quick ASCII sketch of GPU util (approx):
Time -> |--pulse--|---fade(gradual)--|----recovery----|
GPU%:   96  98 100 95  80  64  52  46  44  41  45  60  75  90

Initial notes / thoughts:
- Not a simple cache miss storm: kv_hit% only dips a couple points, not catastrophic.
- GPU util drop while queue_depth is non-zero suggests tasks are entering slow path (context switching, preemption, or device-level stalls).
- p99 spikes correspond with the initial fade, then partially improve but remain > baseline until recovery completes.
- Observed a secondary rise in CPU-side scheduling events concurrently (node-level dmesg shows occasional Kworker slowness during window).

Controlled variations tried so far:
1) Increase batch_timeout_ms -> 12ms
   - Effect: fade magnitude reduced (p99 peak ~340ms vs 430ms) but recovery still present. Throughput unchanged.
2) Lower max_batch_size -> 64
   - Effect: slightly lower p99 during pulse but fade still happens earlier; GPU util drop less abrupt.
3) Pin requests to a single replica during pulse (routing experiment)
   - Effect: isolates pulse to one machine; faded behavior still appears across replicas after pulse ends (implies cluster-level coupling or shared infra limit).
4) Disable preemption (disable kernel preemption on nodes for test pool)
   - Effect: slightly better tail performance but longer recovery duration.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Device warmup hysteresis: during high instantaneous load, some device kernels switch to a different execution path (e.g., larger temp buffers, fallback kernels) and GC / memory compaction runs afterwards causing sustained slowdown.
B) Host-level IO/backpressure: NVMe/PCIe completion queues get bursty and then cause delayed interrupts / scheduling, lowering gpu_util.
C) Scheduler-induced fairness: our autoscaler / admission control temporarily rebalances streams and moves some tasks off fast lanes causing transient underuse until tokens drain.
D) OS-level periodic tasks (kworker/kswapd) triggered by pulse -> causes CPU stalls that delay GPU queue submissions for tens of seconds.

Data to collect next (must instrument):
- Per-device kernel selection logs (which kernel variants were used) + timings per-kernel during pulse
- PCIe/NVMe latencies and interrupt rates in the window
- Per-process scheduling latency histogram on host (task wakeup to run)
- Batch composition trace (which requests coalesced, prefix lengths)
- Fine-grained SLO traces: correlate request id -> which replica served it -> exact timestamps for queue_enqueue, batch_build_start, kernel_launch, token_emit

Immediate mitigation experiments to try (cheap):
- Add a short backoff throttle on ingress after high instantaneous QPS for ~20s (soft shaping) to see if removing the harsh pulse prevents the fade.
- Force kernel selection to 'fast' variant (if available) for one test to see if fade is kernel-choice related.
- Increase pad / prefetch window to keep device memory layout more stable across bursts.

Quick wins observed so far:
- Doubling batch_timeout reduced p99 spike by ~20% during the initial fade window (lessened the worst tail) but didn't eliminate the follow-on degraded util.
- Routing pulse to single replica reduced cluster-wide saturation but didn't prevent the fade propagating (so not purely per-replica cache pressure).

Anomalies and red-flags:
- On one run NVMe latencies spiked to 15ms during fade window (normally <0.5ms). Need more runs to confirm correlation.
- In one test, restarting the runtime process on a single node immediately restored normal behavior on that node while others stayed faded — suggests process-level resource reclamation helps.

Open questions:
- Is this seen on smaller models (rwd-1b) or only >4B? I ran quick rwd-1b and pattern attenuated but still present (shorter fade).
- Is this amplified by quantization artifacts (we run quant-8k)? Try a float16 baseline short test.
- Relationship to our continuous batching heuristics: does batch_pack strategy change after heavy pulses?

Next actions (owners):
- [Sylas] Add kernel-selection trace flags and run 5 controlled pulses across different node types (due: 2026-03-06).
- [Maya] Collect NVMe/PCIe time-series for the same runs and correlate (due: 2026-03-04).
- [Ibrahim] Try ingress soft-shape (10% smoothing for 30s after pulses) in canary pool and measure p99/p999 (due: 2026-03-08).

Notes for later write-up:
- If hypothesis A (kernel switch) is confirmed, we should add an explicit 'kernel warming' path for predicted pulses: keep a small persistent warm batch to avoid kernel fallback after a pulse.
- If B or D confirmed, cluster-level infra remediation (interrupt coalescing parameters, NVMe QoS) required.

Raw commands used (local repro):
- start-replay --trace traces/heavy-tail-15s.json --qps 420 --duration 600 --tag fade-test-1
- runtime-benchctl --set batch_timeout_ms=12 --pool canary-a100
- perf-record --pid $(pgrep runtime) --events sched:sched_wakeup,sched:sched_switch --output run1.perf

End of scratchpad. Keep iterative notes here as experiments run.

-- sylas
